title: sli-cost-latency-ablation-retro-notes-2026
content:
Doc: SLI cost+latency ablation retro notes (working notes -> finalized)
Owner: Priya
Last pass: 2026-03-18 (rolled in post-rollout + follow-up status)

Summary (same study, but these are the messier notes)
----------------------------------------------------
This is the retrospective for the ablation study we ran across late Q4 2025 and early Q1 2026. We intentionally removed/degraded telemetry signals used in the token-latency + cost SLI system to measure sensitivity, false-positive rates, and oncall/operator cognitive load. End goal: concrete runbook changes, dashboard improvements, and rollout guidance to reduce SLI churn during regional blips + model-variant rollouts.

What changed since the Confluence page draft: a few numbers are updated with the final post-rollout window, and we changed the combined paging threshold slightly after the us-east-1 incident review.

Background / why we did this
----------------------------
Context from Oct–Nov 2025:
- Oscillating SLI alerts tied to noisy cost spikes (billing anomalies + reconciliation lag)
- Intermittent token-latency reports that we later correlated with partial KV cache failures
- Oncall time spent correlating: cost panels, latency panels, queue panels, and model variant fallbacks was too manual

Hypothesis (unchanged):
- Some telemetry variants (per-tenant token-cost per-minute derivative, short-window proxy p95) amplify transient noise
- If we ablate secondary/noisy signals and rely on orthogonal indicators (GPU queue length, model-variant error/fallback, KV hit ratio), we reduce alert fatigue without meaningfully increasing time-to-detect real regressions

Study design
------------
Scope/targets:
- Services: routing-proxy, inference-runtime, kv-prefix-cache, cost-aggregator
- SLIs evaluated: token-latency (user-facing tail), token-cost (per-tenant cost rate), request-error-rate, model-variant-fallback-rate

Ablation matrix (same buckets):
- Baseline: full signal set
- Remove short-window p50/p95 at ingress (30s windows)
- Remove per-tenant minute-level cost derivative alert (keep hourly summaries)
- Replace synthetic-sla with synthetic-sla-lite (less frequent)
- Silence KV-hit ratio derived micro-alerts (keep as advisory)

Duration/rollout:
- Canary region: us-west-2 (~2 weeks)
- Staged rollouts: canary -> 3 regions -> global (each stage 72h)
- Automated rollback guard: “detection score” > 0.7 triggers rollback

Timeline + data
---------------
- 2025-11-20 → 2025-12-04: baseline capture
- 2025-12-06 → 2025-12-20: canary ablation (us-west-2)
- 2026-01-05 → 2026-01-19: regional expansion + stress during model-variant rollout
- 2026-01-20 → 2026-02-10: post-rollout monitoring + manual incident injections
- 2026-02-11 → 2026-03-10: “steady state” validation window after global config landed

Data sources:
- Prometheus metrics
- ClickHouse traces
- Billing tables (hourly + per-minute where available)
- Incident tickets + oncall annotations

Key findings (final numbers after steady-state window)
-----------------------------------------------------
1) Short-window proxy p95 removal
- Result: removing 30s ingress p95 from PRIMARY paging reduced page volume by ~46% (was ~43% in earlier analysis)
- Median time-to-detect (verified incidents): moved from 3.8m to 4.3m (earlier draft said 4.2m; steady-state bumped a bit)
- Note: operators still like seeing short-window p95, but only as “fast-sight context” not a pager trigger

2) Minute-level per-tenant cost derivative
- Result: false positives from metering noise down ~81% (earlier: 78%)
- Tradeoff: 1 low-impact cost leak lingered ~9 hours longer than it would have under minute-level paging; detected by hourly delta + routine audit
- Practical conclusion: minute-level derivative can exist, but must be advisory + corroborated

3) KV-hit ratio micro-alerts -> advisory
- Reduced context switching. The pattern we trust now:
  - If KV-hit advisory degradation >5% and GPU queue >12 (NOTE threshold change; see below), tail latency regression tends to follow within ~15–20 minutes
- We should keep KV-hit but stop paging on it alone

4) synthetic-sla-lite coverage
- Still only catches ~60–65% of degradations that affect <5% of traffic
- We should treat synthetic-sla-lite as a “budget saving mode” only if paired with internal health checks

Root cause notes / analysis (messy but keep it)
----------------------------------------------
- Many false positives came from short aggregation windows at proxy:
  - burst traffic patterns
  - backoff storms
  - ingestion/downsampling made micro-bursts look like sustained p95 regressions
- Billing metering noise:
  - quantization + delayed reconciliation between per-token meter and hourly summaries
  - per-minute views were especially spiky during reconciliation lag
- Big operational gap: dashboards didn’t present cross-signal correlation at alert time; oncall manually stitched cost vs latency vs queue vs fallbacks

Decisions made (updated)
------------------------
1) Tail latency SLI
- Keep tail SLI (token-latency p99/p95). Primary paging is based on tail SLI breach, but we no longer page on 30s proxy p95 at all.
- Short-window p95 lives only on “fast-sight” dashboard.

2) Cost derivative
- Per-tenant minute-level cost derivative is advisory only.
- Paging requires corroboration: (billing reconciliation anomaly OR persistent token inflation for 2 consecutive windows) AND at least one service health corroborator.

3) Combined paging rule (threshold adjustment)
- Updated combined-rule: page only when:
  - tail-latency SLI breach AND (gpu-queue > 12 OR model-variant-fallback-rate > 0.5%)
- Earlier draft had gpu-queue > 10; we bumped to 12 after the us-east-1 queue churn review (10 was too sensitive during known batchy periods).

Runbook changes (short list)
----------------------------
- New play: “Cost-Derivative Advisory Investigation” (see below)
- Update: “Tail-Latency Pager” flow includes immediate check of KV-hit advisory + GPU queue before escalation to runtime owners
- Oncall guidance: use fast-sight dashboard for sub-5 min blips; don’t escalate unless corroborating signals exist

Cost-Derivative Advisory Investigation (new play)
------------------------------------------------
1. Watch advisory channel for per-tenant cost spikes.
2. Check hourly summary:
   SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as tokens_hour
   FROM billing.hourly
   WHERE ts >= now() - interval 2 hour
   GROUP BY tenant_id
   ORDER BY tokens_hour DESC
   LIMIT 10;
3. Cross-check same tenant/time window:
   - model-variant fallback rate
   - token-latency p99
4. If token-latency p99 AND cost derivative elevated for >2 windows, open incident and follow standard cost-incident runbook.

Detection scoring + rollback guard
---------------------------------
Still using the same components/weights:
- SLI-breach-rate (0.5)
- new incident count (0.2)
- manual operator escalation (0.2)
- noise ratio penalty (false-alerts / total-alerts) (0.1)

Rollback: if score > 0.7 within 72h.
Note to self: in a future iteration, consider lowering the weight on “incident count” because it’s confounded by unrelated regional issues.

Dashboard + alerting changes (implementation plan + status)
----------------------------------------------------------
Dashboards
- “fast-sight” dashboard: ingress short-window metrics + kv-hit ratio + gpu queue + model-variant fallback + small correlator timeline widget
  - Status: shipped 2026-03-14 (Marcus)
- Cost reconciliation panel: hourly vs per-minute aggregates + reconciliation delta heatmap
  - Status: shipped 2026-03-05 (Diego); this landed earlier than the Confluence timeline
- Panel labeling: tag panels “advisory” vs “primary” to guide attention
  - Status: mostly done; remaining panels are in the cost-aggregator folder

Alerts
- Prometheus rules updated:
  - removed 30s p95 based paging rules
  - implemented combined paging rule (tail latency + gpu queue/fallback)
- Advisory routing:
  - platform-advisory channel (email + Slack thread; no paging)

Operational impact (post-rollout)
---------------------------------
- Page volume (pager count) reduced ~34% across platform owners in steady-state (earlier: 32% during rollout windows)
- MTTA for genuine incidents stable: median 3.9m pre vs 4.2m post
- Operator cognitive load (survey, n=36 after global rollout):
  - 69% reported fewer unnecessary escalations
  - 14% reported slower initial detection on low-impact cost leaks

Follow-ups (updated owners/dates)
--------------------------------
- Platform Observability: fast-sight dashboard
  - Owner: Marcus Green
  - Due: 2026-03-15
  - Status: DONE (2026-03-14)
- Runtime: internal health-check endpoint in inference-runtime to supplement synthetic-sla-lite
  - Owner: Daniela Park
  - Due: 2026-04-08 (slipped from 04-01; resourcing)
  - Status: IN PROGRESS
- Billing: reconciliation job emits reconciliation_delta metric hourly to Prometheus
  - Owner: Diego Alvarez
  - Due: 2026-03-31
  - Status: DONE EARLY (2026-03-05)
- SRE: codify detection scoring + rollback in rollout tooling
  - Owner: Priya Nair
  - Due: 2026-03-24 (moved from 03-10; integrated into shared pipeline)
  - Status: IN REVIEW

Guidelines for future experiments
---------------------------------
- When you ablate a signal, pair it with an orthogonal guardrail (queue length, error rate, reconciliation delta, etc.)
- Detection score should have >= 4 independent-ish components
- Advisory channel reserved for signals that historically cause >60% false positives OR are only actionable with corroboration

Appendix: snippets (copied from earlier, keep for convenience)
------------------------------------------------------------
Ingress short-window p95 query:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30s])) by (le, region))

GPU queue alert snippet (example only; actual threshold now 12 in combined rule):
- alert: GPUQueueHigh
  expr: sum(queue_length) by (region) > 12
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU queue length > 12 (region={{ $labels.region }})"

Reconciliation delta SQL (ClickHouse-ish):
SELECT toHour(ts) as hour, tenant_id,
       sum(per_minute_tokens) as minute_tokens,
       sum(hourly_tokens) as hourly_tokens,
       (hourly_tokens - minute_tokens) as reconciliation_delta
FROM billing.per_minute
JOIN billing.hourly USING (tenant_id, hour)
WHERE ts >= now() - interval 24 hour
GROUP BY hour, tenant_id
ORDER BY reconciliation_delta DESC
LIMIT 50;

Open questions (leaving here; not all resolved)
----------------------------------------------
- Can we auto-annotate alerts with “likely category”: billing noise vs proxy burst vs KV degradation vs rollout?
- Should we maintain per-tenant minute derivative for only top-N tenants (cost/impact) to reduce noise further?
- For synthetic-sla-lite: what’s the minimal internal health check set that materially improves coverage without a lot of maintenance?

Conclusion
----------
Ablation confirmed we can reduce noise by de-emphasizing short-window ingress metrics and minute-level per-tenant cost derivative paging, as long as we strengthen orthogonal guardrails (queue/fallback/reconciliation). Net effect: materially fewer pages with only a small increase in time-to-detect, mostly affecting low-impact cost leaks.
